title: Sharp Bounds on Best-Dose Shares for Ordinal Outcomes in Three-Arm Trials
banked_reason: terminal:laundering — the proposal's defining exact-once all-L 16-register facet stream and finite predecessor classification remain explicitly open, while D0 delivered materially weaker staircase, LP-endpoint, and honesty results.
gap_reasons: The proposal's headline object—an explicit CHECK_2BTAS-accepted exact-once all-L facet stream with a finite predecessor classification—remains an open question; the proved staircase family and scalar transport results are materially weaker substitute deliverables.
The defining all-L sound/complete/unique facet stream remains open and the bounded upgrade is to solve that entire original bottleneck.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 attempted the promised all-L two-pass affine-stream classification while also deriving a staircase facet family, exact finite LP endpoint machinery, sparse attaining mixtures, rates, and finite-sample simultaneous inference. The defining exact-once 16-register stream, finite predecessor types, and unconditional transfer recurrence remained open after both D0.5 panels; solving them is the original research bottleneck rather than a bounded repair.
tldr: Randomization identifies the three marginals of a prespecified ordinal benefit-risk score but not the population shares for which each dose is uniquely best.  Under weak individual unimodality, the compatible target vectors form a structured three-marginal polytope.  The staircase family with \(3^{L-3}\) weighted facets, the exact small-support counts \(59\), \(197\), and \(721\), and sharp endpoint formulas using at most three full facets are proved.  Independently of any all-support facet stream, a finite legal-incidence program computes all six scalar endpoints exactly in polynomial time for rational input, constructs endpoint-attaining rational mixtures with support at most \(3L-2\), and the \(L=2\) equal-Bernoulli example proves that this support bound is uniformly sharp.  Fixed-\(L\) plug-in rates and exact finite-sample simultaneous endpoint coverage, including zero cells and realized empty arms, are also proved.  The remaining mathematical questions are the all-\(L\) exact-once stream with its finite predecessor and transfer classification, and regular-face equivalence of the exact scalar procedure to a specified efficient Wald interval.  The Goodwin et al. application remains an abstract conditional sensitivity analysis: the trial identifies score marginals but neither identifies nor clinically validates weak individual unimodality.
gap: Russell (2021) sharply bounds continuous functionals of the joint law of two potential outcomes in a binary-treatment model, Chiba (2017) bounds and develops randomization inference for \(P\{Y(1)\ge Y(0)\}\) with two ordinal potential outcomes, and Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen (2024) derive sharp symbolic ordinal-benefit formulas in two-arm designs. Generic discrete causal optimizers and multi-marginal transport solvers return numerical values. None classifies the primitive supporting inequalities of the three-dose non-valley coupling polytope for every finite ordinal support, proves a finite predecessor calculus, or compiles such a calculus into an exact-once bounded-register stream; the three-facet endpoint result addresses a unique-best indicator whose forbidden-support geometry is invisible in every two-arm projection.
fill: The project isolates tight-product extremizer and rank signatures, seeks a finite renormalized predecessor classification, and requires a literal \(\texttt{CHECK\_2BTAS}\)-accepted source whose soundness, completeness, and uniqueness are mathematical claims. The same representation is then projected to sharp unique-best endpoints and coupled to exact multinomial inference with an explicit regular-face efficiency target.
